title: Uniqueness of identity
prompt: Prove a group has a unique identity element.

solution.text: Let e and f both be identities.
Since e is an identity, e*f=f. Since f is an identity, e*f=e.
Thus e=f, proving uniqueness.

conceptNote: Associativity changes parentheses, not factor order. Multiply by inverses on the correct side and prove closure before calling a subset a subgroup.

title: Uniqueness of inverse
prompt: If a*b=e in a group, prove b=a^(-1).

solution.text: Left multiply a*b=e by a^(-1): a^(-1)*(a*b)=a^(-1)*e.
Associativity gives (a^(-1)*a)*b=a^(-1).
Hence e*b=a^(-1), so b=a^(-1).

title: Union of subgroups can fail
prompt: Show a union of two subgroups need not be a subgroup.

solution.text: In (Z,+), take H=2Z and K=3Z; both are subgroups.
The numbers 2 and 3 belong to H union K.
But 2+3=5 is in neither 2Z nor 3Z, so the union is not closed under addition.
Therefore H union K need not be a subgroup.

title: Intersection of subgroups
prompt: Prove H intersection K is a subgroup if H,K are subgroups of G.

solution.text: The identity belongs to both H and K, so the intersection is nonempty.
If x,y are in H intersection K, then x*y^(-1) is in H and in K by their subgroup properties.
Thus x*y^(-1) belongs to the intersection. By the subgroup test it is a subgroup.

subject: dm
title: A cancellation-like condition
prompt: Suppose a group satisfies: for every x,y,z, x*y=z*x implies y=z. Prove the group is abelian.

solution.text: Choose arbitrary x,y in the group, and put z=x*y*x^(-1).
Then z*x=(x*y*x^(-1))*x=x*y by associativity and inverse laws.
The assumed implication yields y=z=x*y*x^(-1). Right multiply by x to obtain y*x=x*y.
Since x,y were arbitrary, every pair commutes and the group is abelian.
